findings.text: the head arm's header line names the base revision 6a104b893df8dc5129593a9116353d72465c04cc while the arm measured 3209ea006, and logs/dpr-gate.log:1 and logs/dpr-negative-control.log:1 name the base revision too; reckon/crew/review.py:1245 records that header as head_log_revision, so every read of this review carries a head revision that disagrees with reviewed_head_sha and the node's own requirement that each log be headed with the revision it ran at is unmet for the three head-side logs.

the arm over every file importing reckon.crew.dispatch or reckon.crew.placement, which the done-when names as the population for the 0-added figure, was stopped at about 40% and its header carries an empty module field; the cited after_suite arm stands in over 13 files, so the figure is measured over a narrower population than the measure names (disclosed in the manifest's evidence_inputs, and the stop itself was the instructed response to /tmp under the 5 GB floor).

the suite observations record a template command rather than the command that ran ('--basetemp=<run>/bt-head <same files> plus tests/test_dispatch_places_into_the_shared_reservation.py', against the log's own command line, which carries no --basetemp) and an abbreviated revision ('3209ea006'), and while the run is unarmed (suite_command is null in the live pointer, so promotion.py:3989 skips the suite-delta gate) an armed promotion would refuse it, because promotion.py:4012 compares baseline_suite.revision with the pointer's full base_sha by exact string equality.

the call site that makes placement resolution hold the reservation -- the change the plan's section exists to make -- is asserted by no test: no test file both declares a placement and drives the dispatch entry point, and every placed-wrapping assertion calls resolve_backend_placement or apply_backend_placement directly (tests/test_crew_placement.py:51,65,75,91, tests/test_crew_lane_agnostic_placement.py:208, tests/test_placement_steps_under_reservation.py:135), so reverting this line to apply_backend_placement restores the per-worker minting with the suite still green.

the bare step-client fallback the plan's section asks to replace is still present in apply_backend_placement and reachable by any future direct caller, whereas production now reaches it only through resolve_backend_placement, which always ensures first; the choice is deliberate and stated in the reviewed manifest, but a caller that reaches the wrapper directly mints an allocation per worker silently, which is the defect this node removed from the dispatch path.

item_verdicts.diff: read against base 6a104b893: 380 insertions and 10 deletions over five files, dispatch.py gaining the resolver and changing the call at :4911, the replacement test stating the ensure, the new file holding the four cases, and the retry assertion becoming a literal.
item_verdicts.done_when: the four cases the done-when names are the four tests at tests/test_dispatch_places_into_the_shared_reservation.py:144,170,197,216, the gate log records '4 passed' with EXIT=0, and the two arms record 3 pre-existing failures with 134 passed at base and 138 at head, so the added-failure count is 0.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that placement resolution holds or joins the one shared reservation through ensure_reservation, and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6018 adds resolve_backend_placement which calls placement.ensure_reservation before delegating to the existing wrapper, with dispatch.py:4911 its only production caller.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states status complete, names the gate log and both arm logs, records 0 added failures and no attribution, and discloses both the /tmp-truncated importing-set arm and the wrapper's bare branch left in place.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths were read from the manifest; git diff --name-only across the base and head lists exactly five paths and every one is declared, with reckon/crew/placement.py and the figures directory declared and untouched.

justifications.durability: tests/test_dispatch_places_into_the_shared_reservation.py:188 fails under the declared mutation (logs/dpr-negative-control.log records assert 2 == 1 with EXIT=1) and is independent of the value under test because it counts the recording scheduler's own log, but no test drives dispatch() with a placed backend, so the wiring at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4911 is unguarded.
justifications.evidence: the gate and both arms are recorded and reconcile -- 4 passed with EXIT=0, and the two arms carry the same three failure ids (134 passed at base, 138 at head) so the added count is 0 -- but all three head-side logs open with the base revision (logs/dpr-gate.log:1, logs/dpr-delta-head-placement.log:1, logs/dpr-negative-control.log:1) and the importing-set arm the done-when names stands unfinished at about 40%.
justifications.fit: the resolver follows the module's existing idiom -- a lazy import as at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5981, a docstring stating the mechanism rather than the incident, and delegation to the existing wrapper instead of a second implementation -- and introduces no symbol or comment carrying a plan, stage or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4911 is the only production caller, so a dispatch declaring a placement reaches placement.ensure_reservation (reckon/crew/placement.py:418, under the cross-process lock) before the wrapper reads the published record at dispatch.py:6002, and a second project therefore joins the one allocation rather than minting another while a backend declaring no placement returns untouched at dispatch.py:6041.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 6a104b893..3209ea006 lists exactly five paths and every one is inside the manifest's declared write paths, and the literal retry assertion in tests/test_ensure_holds_one_reservation.py:214 is named in the node's own done-when rather than carried in from elsewhere.
